StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single, sim does not override on_stack, so it adds -- matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236). The Amount IS read here (it is the reattach heal, ReattachPower.cs:47 / powers.py:3004-3005), which is precisely why leaving on_stack alone matters; monsters/hive/decimillipede.py applies it once per segment.

AfterDeath.rationale: The one unit in this family the sim gets STRUCTURALLY right: it uses the real after-death hook (hooks.on_death, cmds.py:162) plus should_remove_from_combat_after_death, so the segment genuinely dies at 0 HP and is retained, exactly as C# does -- and combat.py's `_resolve_death`-adjacent comment says so outright ("a corpse the combat retained (a withered Decimillipede segment) keeps taking turns -- that is how it reaches REATTACH"). Guard-for-guard: `wasRemovalPrevented || base.Owner != creature` -> `creature is not self.owner or self.is_reviving` (powers.py:2986; see the wasRemovalPrevented guard below), and `!AreAllOtherSegmentsDead() || !base.Owner.IsDead` -> `if self._all_others_down(): return` (powers.py:2988-2989). The `|| !base.Owner.IsDead` arm is dropped, which is defensive only: on this path the owner is always dead. The else-branch (DoFadeOutOnAllSegments) is pure presentation.

ShouldAllowHitting.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: PowerCmd.apply (cmds.py:853) opens with `if not can_receive_powers(hooks, target): return None` (cmds.py:901), and `can_receive_powers` (cmds.py:65-75) is `not target.is_removed_from_combat and hooks.should_allow_hitting(target)` -- the sim's port of PowerCmd.Apply<T>'s `if (!target.CanReceivePowers) return null` (PowerCmd.cs:73-76), whose CanReceivePowers reuses Hook.ShouldAllowHitting (Creature.cs:308-322). WAS: the predicate was wired into DamageCmd.deal only (cmds.py:311-312), so a debuff landed on a creature the game refuses to touch -- Vulnerable sticking to a reviving Test Subject.

ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.rationale: `creature != base.Owner -> true, else false` maps exactly to `return creature is not self.owner`. This is the only power in half B that uses the sim's real hook for it, and it is why the Decimillipede works: cmds.py:158-160 sets `retained_after_death = not should_remove_from_combat_after_death(...)` and combat.py:737 then keeps the corpse taking turns.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath.rationale: `ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath() => false`. C# strips a dead creature's powers at CreatureCmd.cs:533 (`creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath()`, then each power's AfterRemoved) and this override opts out so the power survives the death it is supposed to react to. RE-READ THIS PASS, AND THE PREMISE HAS CHANGED SINCE THIS RECORD WAS WRITTEN: the sim NOW strips powers after death for real. `_strip_powers_after_death` (cmds.py:223-238) is called from the real-death arm of `_resolve_death` and does exactly the C# thing -- `doomed = [p for p in target.powers.values() if p.should_power_be_removed_after_owner_death() and hooks.should_power_be_removed_on_death(p)]`, then `_expire()` + `on_removed` for each -- so ReattachPower's `False` override is no longer 'satisfied for free', it is now the thing that actively keeps this power alive on its own owner's death, exactly matching C#. This appears to CLOSE the previously-recorded engine-level sibling gap at `audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json` step 8b (last known as `gap`, LIVE, 'the sim strips no powers on death') -- that record is seam-owned and out of my batch, so I have NOT edited it, but flagging for the controller: `_strip_powers_after_death` existing and being wired into `_resolve_death`'s real-death arm looks like it closes 8b. Faithful HERE either way, since this power's own override behaves correctly under both the old and the new model.

ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): `PowerModel.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal` EXISTS in the sim now. `Power.should_owner_death_trigger_fatal` defaults to True (PowerModel.cs:646) and the two non-mock overrides are ported at their own sites -- MinionPower unconditionally (MinionPower.cs:20-23) and ReattachPower as `_all_others_down()` (ReattachPower.cs:106-109, whose own comment says "shouldn't trigger fatal unless all other segments are dead too"). `cmds.should_trigger_fatal(target)` is the `Target.Powers.All(...)` test, and BOTH Fatal cards call it BEFORE their attack, which is where C# reads it and is load-bearing: the killing blow strips the very powers the test asks about (Creature.RemoveAllPowersAfterDeath). This is NOT death prevention -- the minion really dies -- which is exactly why the `is_dead` check both cards already had did not cover it. ReattachPower's override reuses the power's own `_all_others_down()`, which is `AreAllOtherSegmentsDead` -- so killing the LAST standing segment does trigger Fatal and killing any earlier one does not.  Pinned by test/test_card_residue_gaps.py.  NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: Same missing hook as MinionPower's, and here the override is CONDITIONAL: `ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal() => AreAllOtherSegmentsDead()` (ReattachPower.cs:106-109), so killing a segment while others stand must NOT trigger a Fatal payoff and killing the last one must. The sim has no hook and cards/feed.py:45 tests only `target.is_dead`, which is True for a withered segment (it really sits at 0 HP -- the sim's own `_all_others_down` comment says so, powers.py:2334-2336). So Feed on a non-final segment grants +3 max HP in the sim and 0 in the game. LIVE by the same executed witness as power/minion's (Feed x a Minion-marked creature, delta 3 vs 0); reachability here is the ported Hive Decimillipede (monsters/hive/decimillipede.py) plus the ported Rare Ironclad Feed. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: CORRECTION worth writing down, because the parameter is misnamed in the decompiled source and the obvious reading is wrong: `wasRemovalPrevented: true` is passed when **Hook.ShouldDie returned FALSE**, i.e. when the DEATH was prevented (CreatureCmd.cs:566), and `false` on the path where the creature really dies (CreatureCmd.cs:519). It is NOT about ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath, which is computed separately at CreatureCmd.cs:508 and does not feed the flag. So `!wasRemovalPrevented` means "the creature actually died". RE-READ THIS PASS: the sim's `_resolve_death` (cmds.py:126-220) NOW calls `hooks.on_death` on BOTH branches -- the real-death arm at cmds.py:162 (`hooks.on_death(target, False)`) and the prevented arm at cmds.py:219 (`hooks.on_death(target, True)`) -- unlike the earlier structure this rationale used to describe, where the prevented branch never dispatched AfterDeath at all. ReattachPower.on_death (powers.py:2981-2991) itself does NOT test its `was_removal_prevented` parameter, only `creature is not self.owner or self.is_reviving`, so on paper a prevented death would still wither the segment. DORMANT, executed by reading rather than a probe: `hooks.should_die` (hooks.py:1872-1880) only has two registered listeners in the whole sim -- `LizardTailPower.should_die_late` and the Fairy-in-a-Bottle-equivalent potion's `should_die` (potions.py:1394-1395, `return creature.side != "player"`, i.e. it vetoes ONLY when `creature.side == "player"`) -- both player-only relics/potions, and grep of every monster package for a `should_die` override returns none. ReattachPower's owner is always an enemy (a Decimillipede segment), so the prevented branch of `_resolve_death` is never reached for it; `was_removal_prevented` arrives as `False` on every call this power's owner can ever receive. Named trigger: an enemy-side death-prevention listener (none ported) or Reattach applied to a player (never happens; the applier is the Hive Decimillipede monster only). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

C# filters `GetTeammatesOf(Owner).Except([Owner]).Where(c => c.HasPower<ReattachPower>())` and asks `.All(s => s.IsDead)`; powers.py:2962-2974 filters `combat.enemies` for `e is not self.owner and "reattach" in e.powers` and asks `all(s.is_dead ...)`. Equivalent in single-player (teammates of an enemy == the enemy list), and the vacuous-truth case matches too: a lone segment gets `all([]) == True` on both sides, which is what makes killing the last one final.

powers.py:2998-3001 reproduces it, comment included. The heal differs in FORM -- C# calls `CreatureCmd.Heal(Owner, base.Amount)` (heal BY Amount, capped at max HP) where powers.py:3004-3005 SETS `hp = self.amount` -- but the segment is at 0 HP when it reattaches, so heal-by-N and set-to-N coincide. Recorded because they would not coincide if anything ever healed a withered segment first, and nothing does.

No C# counterpart is needed -- C# never removed the creature -- but the sim must clear the flag it set at cmds.py:158-160 or the revived segment would keep being treated as a corpse. Correct, and load-bearing.
